question: When a thin beam of white light is passed through a prism then:
solution:
The correct answer is __**light will disperse**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Dispersion of light: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/638ec4dc30fa2a16b08c5254d67b8b4a7a601c7a75b4c1f665c95578cb9d0c72.png] 

 
• The white light is formed by seven visible colours called VIBGYOR. (Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red).
 
• Dispersion of light is the phenomenon of splitting of a beam of white light into its constituent colours when passing through a prism.
 
• The band of seven colours so obtained is called the (visible) spectrum. 
 
• Dispersion of white light occurs because the colours of white light travel at different speeds through the glass prism.
 
• All colours have different wavelengths. 
 
• Light bends when its travels from one medium to another. So, it bends when it travels from air to the prism. 
 
• The light with the least wavelength bends the most. Red bends the least as it has a maximum wavelength and violet bends the most. 
 
• The white light is formed by seven visible colours called VIBGYOR. Among these, the light bent the most after Violet is Indigo following the sequence VIBGYOR. 
 
• So, the light which will bend most is Violet. and least is Red.
